summary: Tatiana Oranskaia specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1968–1973) and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (1988). She held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996, 1998–2016).

Tatsugen Sato worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology, completing his doctorate at Komazawa University by 1978. He served as assistant professor (~1970–1995) and professor (~1976–1995) at Komazawa University, and also taught at Tokai University and Ryukoku University (attested 1974).

Tatsuo Hayashi was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1921). He held academic posts at Hosei University (~1926–1932), Toyo University (~1928–1944), Meiji University (~1932–1944), Tsuda University (~1948–1968), and Rikkyo University.

Tatsuo Nishida worked in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology, earning his doctorate at Kyoto University, where he studied from 1948 to 1962. He was a professor and dean at Kyoto University, served at NACSIS (1992–1994), and chaired the LSJ (1979–1981).

Tavivat Puntarigvivat specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and under Luangpor Teean Jittasubho. He held posts at Kyoto University, Mahidol University (attested 2005), and World Buddhist University (attested 2013).
Taw Sein Ko was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Rangoon (~1880–1882), the Inner Temple (~1892–1894), and the Inns of Court (~1892–1894).

Tawni Tidwell is a Tibetologist who earned her Ph.D. from Emory University (2009–2017). She held postdoctoral and research associate positions at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2018–2019), the University of Vienna (2019), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2019).

Teizo Iyanaga specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1936–1939) and later held posts at Nagoya University (~1948–1950), the University of Tokyo (~1950–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).

Tej Ram Sharma is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Banaras Hindu University by 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (attested 1978).
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under Lobsang Gyatso and the 14th Dalai Lama, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.
Tenga Rinpoche was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Benchen Monastery, served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1967–1983), and founded Benchen Monastery in 1976.

Tensei Kitabatake was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1948–1955). He served Ryukoku University from 1955 to 1999 as lecturer, professor, and president, and later was president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded Sogen Omori, and founded Chozen-ji.

Tenzin Dorjee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Geshe Dawa. He worked as a translator at the LTWA and served at Pullahari Monastery (attested 2000).

Tenzin Namdak is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shes rab bstan 'dzin rgyal mtshan, sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan, and Lobpön Tsultrim Gyaltsen, earning a degree at Menri Monastery. He founded Triten Norbutse Monastery.

Tenzin Namgha specializes in Tibetology, earning a Ph.D. at Christ University (2010–2016). He held roles at the Dalai Lama Institute for Higher Education (2019–2021), Central Tibetan Administration (2021), and York University (2026).

Tenzin Norbu specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held a post at Columbia University and serves as an assistant professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Tenzin Tsenyi works in Tibetology and religious studies. She is a doctoral student and assistant at the University of Warsaw (attested 2026), where she also held an assistant-academic teacher post (2024–2025).

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sangye Tenzin and Tenzin Namdak, earning a Geshe degree at Menri Monastery (~1975–1986). He directed Menri's Dialectic School (~1986–1991) and founded Ligmincha International.

Teodor Iordănescu was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Bucharest (~1893–1897) and at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1901–1903) under Richard Pischel, Richard Schmidt, and Eugen Hultzsch.
